scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A familiar page
scenes.caption: Kabir receives a festival link. The page has a school crest and a familiar title, and it asks him to sign in. Those page details can be copied. He needs to inspect what the browser actually opened.
scenes.dialogue: The page looks familiar. What does the address say?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Read the address
scenes.caption: The hostname begins with the school name but continues into another domain. The known school hostname is different. A familiar word inside an address does not mean that the whole address belongs to that organisation.
scenes.dialogue: Read all the way to the next slash.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Connection limits
scenes.caption: H T T P S protects the connection to the hostname shown. It does not establish that the operator is your school or that a request is honest. An independent known address or school contact helps verify the claim.
scenes.dialogue: A protected connection is not an endorsement.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Your decision
scenes.caption: Identify the full hostname in the supplied address bar. Start after the scheme and stop at the next slash. Do not use the page title, logo or only the familiar beginning.
scenes.dialogue: Which hostname did we really open?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Independent route
scenes.caption: Kabir uses the school address from his diary and checks through the school instead of replying to the suspicious sender. He does not type credentials into the supplied page. He records the evidence and its limits.
scenes.dialogue: I will use a route I already know.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the lab
scenes.caption: A programme page also asks for access to contacts. Displaying festival times does not need the whole contact list. In the lab, read full hostnames, explain connection indicators and make a proportionate permission decision.
scenes.dialogue: Check both the destination and the request.
